content:
Here’s why web design and UX matter more than people think.

2 min read
Just now

--

You know what’s one of my biggest icks? When I click on a website and it takes forever to load. No wait, it’s when I’m ambushed with fifteen options before I can even see the page. No, actually, it’s when the whole thing feels like a scavenger hunt and I didn’t sign up to play. Clearly I have several icks when it comes to website design, and I’d bet you do too.
Websites matter more than people give them credit for. A good one can make a brand, and a bad one can break it just as fast. I think a lot of people don’t fully get the gravity of web design and UX, and it’s usually because they’re confusing it with UI. UI is how you navigate a site, UX is how it makes you feel while you’re using it. Two different things, and both matter.
So let’s do a quick crash course.
Quick definition before we get into it, “stickiness” is a real marketing term for how well a website keeps people around instead of bouncing off it. That’s the whole point of this post, lol anyway.
